title: Enable or disable a network interface
summary: Turn a network interface on or off using ifconfig. This is useful for troubleshooting or temporarily disconnecting from a network.

steps.explain: To disable an interface, use the 'down' keyword. This requires root privileges.

placeholders.name: INTERFACE_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the network interface, e.g., eth0, wlan0.

alternatives.explain: To enable an interface, use the 'up' keyword.

placeholders.name: INTERFACE_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the network interface, e.g., eth0, wlan0.

alternatives.explain: Use `sudo ip link set` followed by the interface name and `up` or `down` to change its state.

placeholders.name: INTERFACE
placeholders.description: The name of the network interface (e.g., eth0, wlan0).

placeholders.name: STATE
placeholders.description: The desired state: 'up' to enable, 'down' to disable.

rollback.explain: To re-enable the interface if you disabled it, use the 'up' command.

placeholders.name: INTERFACE_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the network interface.

warnings: Disabling an interface will disconnect you from the network associated with it. Ensure you have another way to access the system if you are working remotely.
